name: RAD-140 (testolone)

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Breast cancer models; mouse muscle and bone

track.title: Research use only
track.line: Sold labelled not for human use; FDA: unapproved

what.text: RAD-140 (also written RAD140, and called testolone) is a nonsteroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM). In lab and mouse models of breast cancer that have both androgen and estrogen receptors, it slowed tumour growth.

src.label: Yu et al., Clin Cancer Res, 2017

what.text: Its only published human trial was a small first-in-human study in women with breast cancer. It is not an approved medicine. FDA considers SARM products sold online unapproved drugs.

src.label: LoRusso et al., Clin Breast Cancer, 2022
FDA consumer update: FDA warns of use of SARMs among teens, young adults

what.text: RAD-140 has never been tested in a trial in men. It is not FDA approved and is banned in sport.

research.text: One published human trial exists: a Phase 1 safety study in 22 women with advanced breast cancer. There are no trials in men. Most other human reports are case reports of harm in people who used products sold as RAD-140.

research.title: First-in-human study in metastatic breast cancer (LoRusso et al.)

facts.v: open-label, dose-escalation Phase 1 study (3 + 3 design) with a drug-level expansion group; registry NCT03088527
22 heavily pretreated postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer
safety, tolerated dose, drug levels, tumour response

research.found: Grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 16 of 22 women (72.7%), including raised liver enzymes (AST/ALT) in 22.7%. Raised AST occurred in 59.1% and ALT in 45.5% overall. One woman had a partial response; median progression-free survival was 2.3 months. The registry lists Stemline Therapeutics as sponsor.

src.label: LoRusso et al., Clin Breast Cancer, 2022
ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03088527

research.text: In young male rats, 14 days of RAD-140 increased muscle fibre size without changing bone. In female mice, 10 weeks of RAD-140 increased frailty and mortality risk and did not improve strength. These results are in animals only.

src.label: Puskas et al., Physiol Rep, 2025 (rats)
Brown et al., Clin Exp Pharmacol Physiol, 2023 (female mice)

us.text: RAD-140 is not FDA approved for any use. Products labelled “research use only” are unapproved drugs, and FDA does not allow them to be sold for people to take. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: FDA says that although SARMs are often marketed as dietary supplements or “sold for research use only,” they are considered unapproved drugs, and SARMs cannot be legally marketed in the US as a dietary supplement or a drug at this time. FDA also notes that products labelled “for research purposes” or “not for human consumption” have been sold directly to consumers for human use. FDA does not allow these products to be sold for people to take.

side.text: Raised liver enzymes were the most common side effect in the only trial. Published case reports describe serious liver injury, and heart problems, in people who used products sold as RAD-140.

items.text: in the 22-woman Phase 1 study, raised AST (59.1%), ALT (45.5%) and bilirubin (27.3%), vomiting, dehydration, and lower appetite and weight were common. Grade 3 or 4 events occurred in 72.7%.

src.label: LoRusso et al., Clin Breast Cancer, 2022

items.text: a 24-year-old man developed jaundice and cholestatic liver injury after 5 weeks of RAD-140, with bilirubin peaking at 38.5 mg/dL; it resolved after stopping. A 52-year-old man developed liver injury after products containing RAD-140 and LGD-4033; liver tests returned to normal about 3 months after stopping. Severe liver injury after RAD-140 has also been reported in Australia.

items.text: FDA lists serious or life-threatening problems linked to SARMs in studies and reports: higher risk of heart attack or stroke, psychosis and hallucinations, sleep problems, sexual dysfunction, liver injury and acute liver failure, infertility, miscarriage and testicular shrinkage. FDA says liver injuries needing hospital care have occurred.

items.text: Health Canada links SARMs to drug-induced liver damage, heart attack and stroke, changes in blood lipids, fluid retention, thicker blood, and hormone disruption that can lead to infertility, lower sex drive, sexual dysfunction and breast enlargement in men.

src.label: Health Canada public advisory on seized unauthorized health products, including SARMs

items.text: SARMs act on the androgen receptor. Like testosterone, they can lower the body’s own testosterone and the hormones that drive sperm production. FDA and Health Canada both list infertility among the risks.
